content.comment_body: I'm developing a program to measure spacing between objects on a conveyor belt. If two objects are closer than the required spacing, I want to reject both. I'm struggling to achieve this with the available single sensor. Any advice to help implement this logic?
Please upload your program as a ZIP file so others can review it.

Hello, I'm a bit unclear on your exact requirements. How do you want to reject the two objects, and what happens afterward? Can you provide more details? For now, I would use the sensor's negative signal—if the negative state lasts longer than a set timer value, the spacing between bottles is correct. If less, then rejection should occur.
What is the correct time interval between two bottles when the spacing is acceptable?

Thanks for your response. I've attached the program I created and have solved the spacing issue. Now I have another problem—when trying to adjust timer or counter settings, the option to reference another function is missing.
How do you set up references between function blocks in [product_name] [version_no]?
If you press the plus button below a block, you'll see additional connection options for that block.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on configuring logic to control spacing between conveyor objects with one sensor, highlighting the challenge of object rejection based on measured distance. After the main logic is addressed, a usability issue arises when adjusting timer or counter values due to missing user interface elements for function block references. This points to difficulties with both feature implementation and interface clarity in the programming software.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to easily develop logic to measure distances and manage object rejection. They also anticipate that the programming software will offer simple, intuitive tools for adjusting timers, counters, and configuring references between function blocks.
